correctness.rationale: Assari--Hosseinzadeh--Macpherson's full primary text defines \(M_3\) from the strongly dense ordered binary \(C\)-set, proves \(\operatorname{Aut}(M_3)=\operatorname{Aut}(M,C,<)\), and in the set-homogeneity proof identifies the unique left/right root-cone decomposition. A finite type is therefore a plane full binary tree. For a root split with \(i\) leaves left and \(j=n-i\) right, every cross triple with one left and two right leaves is an edge and the other cross orientation is not, contributing exactly \(i\binom j2\); this gives the recurrence. Root reflection complements every triple, giving palindromy. The support induction is valid after the explicit five- and six-leaf base cases because the intervals contributed by the \((n-1,1)\) and \((1,n-1)\) splits overlap. An independent reconstruction of the recurrence through \(n=10\) produced Catalan totals, the stated five-leaf gap, complete support from \(n=6\), and palindromy in every checked degree.
correctness.risk: The unrefined Catalan profile of the underlying ordered tree is classical; correctness of the refined statement depends on using the precise orientation convention in the source definition of \(M_3\).

final_claim: For the set-homogeneous 3-hypergraph \(M_3\), the edge-refined finite-type enumerator satisfies \(P_1(q)=1\) and \(P_n(q)=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}q^{i\binom{n-i}{2}}P_i(q)P_{n-i}(q)\). Hence \(P_n(1)=C_{n-1}\), \(P_n(q)=q^{\binom n3}P_n(q^{-1})\), the five-vertex edge spectrum is \(\{0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10\}\), and every edge count from \(0\) to \(\binom n3\) occurs for every \(n\ge6\); the number of injective ordered \(n\)-tuple orbits is \(n!C_{n-1}\).
limitations: The claim does not assert analogous edge spectra for the other set-homogeneous hypergraphs \(M_4,M_6,N_3\).
